runPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production game sprite animation sheet.
Create EXACTLY 24 complete full-body running poses of the SAME Reaper from the reference artwork, facing RIGHT, in a strict 6-column by 4-row equal-cell grid, reading left-to-right top-to-bottom. Use a wide 3:2 canvas, ideally 3072 x 2048. Transparent background, generous invisible gutters. No text, numbers, scenery, cast shadows, decorative particles, grid lines, or motion trails.
The input images are reference images for the approved identity and costume: ivory skull, one bright cyan eye under dark hood, bronze shoulder armor and boots, black robe with burgundy torn inner cloak, large ornate skull scythe with one curved pointed blade. Match the original hand-painted gothic storybook outlines, colors, material detail and proportions precisely.
This is one mechanically coherent COMPLETE two-step running cycle, not 24 independent concepts. Character body size and camera stay the same in all 24 cells. Each full character INCLUDING the scythe and cloak fits completely inside its cell with 8% margins; no touching neighboring cells. Boot ground baseline at 90% of each cell, pelvis root at 60% cell width. Gait is purposeful, agile, slightly forward leaning and stylish but restrained. Have actual alternating left/right legs, flexing knees and ankles, planted weight, toe push-off and foot clearance; do not slide rigid straight legs back and forth. One hand holds the scythe diagonally over the rear shoulder; free arm counter-swings. Small natural shoulder/hip rotation and restrained rise/fall; cloak tips lag the body and ripple smoothly through the loop. Consistent skull, eye, hands, scythe blade geometry and armor size.
POSE PLAN: frames 1–3 left heel contact ahead and right toe push-off behind, weight settles; 4–6 left support leg moves beneath body and flexes while right knee swings forward; 7–9 left heel lifts and pushes off as right knee leads; 10–12 brief flight then right leg reaches forward, left heel folds up behind; 13–15 right heel contact and left toe push-off, weight settles; 16–18 right support beneath body with left knee swinging forward; 19–21 right push-off and left knee leads; 22–24 brief flight and left leg extends toward next contact, returning naturally to frame 1. All intermediate poses must be visibly distinct, equally spaced through the gait, smoothly progressive and anatomically coherent. Avoid repeating the same extended-leg pose in every frame. Preserve the exact reference character identity.
jumpPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production transparent game sprite animation sheet.
Generate EXACTLY 24 complete full-body poses of the SAME right-facing Reaper in a strict 6 columns x 4 rows equal-cell grid, left-to-right reading order, wide 3:2 image ideally 3072x2048. Every full character, scythe blade and cloak must fit its own cell with transparent gutters. Absolutely no text, labels, shadows on ground, background, particles or grid lines. True transparent alpha.
Input images are approved character identity references. Preserve ivory skull, single cyan eye, black angular hood/robe, bronze shoulder armor/boots, burgundy torn flowing cloak and exact ornate skull scythe. Hand-painted gothic storybook artwork precisely matching references. Keep skull and torso dimensions identical across all 24 drawings. Side-on game camera, right facing. No rotation toward camera.
This is a connected JUMP AND LAND sequence with full natural leg, torso, free-arm, scythe and cloak articulation. The scythe stays gripped securely in the rear hand, carried diagonally over rear shoulder; torso and cloak follow body motion. Keep pelvis in roughly same horizontal location, around 60% cell width. The imaginary character root/foot reference is at 90% cell height. These drawings animate posture only; don't draw a character traveling up the sheet, game physics handles height.
POSES: 1 running push-off preparation with knees compressing slightly; 2 stronger toe push-off; 3 launch and rear leg extends; 4 launch completion with ankle pointing down. 5–8 progressively tuck knees during rising flight and lift free arm naturally. 9–12 approach the apex, legs gently relax with restrained cloak follow-through. 13–16 transition to falling with knees uncurling and boots preparing under the body; cloak tips float briefly upward. 17–18 feet extend toward the ground, knees ready to absorb. 19 first landing contact with front boot; 20 both boots touch and knees bend; 21 deepest soft landing compression with slight forward lean; 22 rise from compression; 23 push into first running step; 24 ready to rejoin running. Contact poses share one boot baseline. All 24 must be distinct, clearly progressive, consistent character scale and costume. No rigid standing poses pasted at different heights. No weapon duplication.
